declared.title: Happiness, income satiation and turning points around the world
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « happiness income satiation turning points around the world » (2026-11-22)

population: Gallup World Poll 2005-2016, 164 countries; MENA region 246,998 people, Egypt 20,924 of them (supplementary tables 1 and 3)

findings.text: Worldwide, satiation at about $95,000 a year for life evaluation and $60,000-75,000 for emotions (household income per person-equivalent, PPP dollars)

support.sentence: Globally, we find that satiation occurs at $95,000 for life evaluation and $60,000 to $75,000 for emotional well-being.

findings.text: The satiation point varies a lot between world regions, and comes later in richer regions

support.sentence: However, there is substantial variation across world regions, with satiation occurring later in wealthier regions.

findings.text: In some parts of the world, incomes beyond the satiation point go with lower life evaluations

support.sentence: We also find that in certain parts of the world, incomes beyond satiation are associated with lower life evaluations.

limits: cross-sectional: an association, not an effect of money
income is household income divided by the square root of its size, in PPP dollars: not comparable as such with Kahneman & Deaton's household $75,000
MENA (SI table 2): satiation at $115,000 for life evaluation, $110,000 positive affect, $125,000 negative affect; 1.14% of the region above $115,000
MENA: no decline beyond satiation (p = .51, SI table 2): the region is not one of the « turning point » regions
no estimate for Egypt alone: its 20,924 respondents are pooled in the MENA region
very few respondents above the satiation points (about 1% worldwide): the flat part rests on thin data
the article itself is paywalled: only the abstract and the supplementary information were read
